issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify acceptSupplyDelivery takes four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity), but the solution implements a static acceptSupplyDelivery with only three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and may cause compilation or test failures if they follow the textual/UML spec instead of the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the signature consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement/UML to require acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (removing the supplier parameter) or modify the solution/template to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and handle or store the supplier parameter accordingly. Ensure tests and documentation are updated to match the chosen signature.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) but the reference implementation defines acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) with only three parameters (missing the supplier parameter). This mismatch between the specified API and the implemented method signature creates a conceptual mapping gap: students reading the problem expect to implement or call a four-parameter method, while the solution uses a different signature and parameter ordering for the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Either update the solution to implement the four-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (and handle or store the supplier parameter), or modify the problem statement to require the three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). Preferably, update the implementation to accept (String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) so it matches the problem description and UML.
